name: Citizenship by Descent (Bill C-3)

requirement_groups.name: Born/adopted abroad BEFORE 15 December 2025 (2nd generation or later)

requirements.blocker_text: This covers a person born or adopted abroad, to a Canadian parent (who was themselves also born abroad), before 15 December 2025 — citizenship is automatically restored/conferred by operation of law, with NO generational cap for this group.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for a citizenship certificate as proof (interim-measure applications are processed under the new rules without re-filing).

requirement_groups.name: Born/adopted abroad ON/AFTER 15 December 2025 (2nd generation or later)

requirements.blocker_text: This covers births/adoptions abroad on or after 15 December 2025 to a Canadian parent who was themselves also born abroad — citizenship requires the Canadian parent to meet a substantial-connection test of at least 1,095 days' physical presence in Canada BEFORE the birth/adoption.
requirements.fix_path: The Canadian parent must document at least 1,095 days of physical presence in Canada before the child's birth/adoption.

evidence_required.document: Birth/adoption certificate and evidence of the Canadian parent's citizenship
Evidence of the Canadian parent's 1,095-day physical presence before the birth (post-cutoff group only)

sources.title: Bill C-3 - IRCC (Royal Assent 20 Nov 2025, in force 15 Dec 2025)

notes: MAJOR LIVE LEGAL EVENT, one of the most significant citizenship-law changes in this entire multi-country research pass: the Ontario Superior Court of Justice declared Canada's 'first-generation limit' on citizenship by descent unconstitutional in December 2023; Bill C-3 (Royal Assent 20 Nov 2025, in force 15 Dec 2025) removed that limit for the affected population. This is genuinely the OPPOSITE direction from Portugal's contemporaneous jure sanguinis restriction — Portugal imposed a NEW generational cap in 2025 while Canada REMOVED an existing one in the same period, a real and striking cross-country contrast worth surfacing prominently in any comparison view of ancestry routes across this dataset. The pre/post 15-Dec-2025 bifurcation is genuinely load-bearing: pre-cutoff 2nd-generation-or-later applicants get automatic restoration with NO cap, while post-cutoff births require the Canadian parent to clear a 1,095-day substantial-connection test — modeled here as two distinct requirement groups rather than one, since collapsing them would misrepresent a materially different legal test. STALE-DATA WARNING confirmed during research: several tier-3 sites (mercan.com, ircc.com [a look-alike commercial domain, NOT the real government site], libertyimmigration.ca, visaverge.com) describe this reform expansively and sometimes inaccurately — claiming reach to 'great-grandparents' or 'millions of Americans automatically eligible.' Only canada.ca should be treated as authoritative for generation-counting specifics.
